title: The Prayer of the Re-Created
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: God as Creator and Re-Creator
subpoints: God is the direct cause of every human conception.
Regeneration transforms the heart of stone into a heart of flesh.
Believers are new creations in Christ.

outline.title: The Purpose of Recreation: Understanding God's Word
subpoints: Regeneration grants the ability to understand Scripture.
Biblical learning involves acting on knowledge.
The recreated person craves and loves God's commandments.

outline.title: Comfort in Covenant Faithfulness (Chesed)
subpoints: God's steadfast love is based on His intra-trinitarian covenant.
God's faithfulness is independent of human performance.
The Bible is the basis for trusting God's promises.

outline.title: Compassion as Life
subpoints: God's tender mercies are His compassion.
The believer finds life and delight in God's law.
Compassion is deeply felt in the believer's being.

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro explores Psalm 119:73-80, highlighting the prayers of a believer who has been spiritually regenerated. The passage begins with the psalmist acknowledging God as both the physical creator and the spiritual re-creator, emphasizing that God is directly involved in the conception and spiritual birth of every human being. This recreation, described as the transformation of a heart of stone into a heart of flesh, is the foundation for the believer's new relationship with God.

The primary purpose of this spiritual recreation is to grant the believer the understanding necessary to learn and live according to God's commandments. The sermon notes that the recreated person possesses a deep craving for Scripture, viewing God's law not as a burden but as a source of delight and meditation. This love for the Word is rooted in the assurance that God communicates His will clearly through the Bible.

Furthermore, the psalmist prays for comfort based on God's covenant faithfulness, or *chesed*. The sermon explains that this steadfast love is grounded in the eternal covenant within the Trinity, ensuring that God's promises remain secure regardless of human failure. Finally, the passage highlights God's compassion as a source of life, illustrating how the believer finds sustenance and joy in the tender mercies of the Lord.
